title: Corrected Throughput Analysis with Run-to-Run Variance

methodology.rationale: T56 ran each config once; T53 vs T56 showed 16% variance for same config (143.5 vs 120.2 TPS). This test runs 3x per config to measure variance.

starvation_reference.cause: Batch starvation: 75 concurrent txns never fill 100+ message blocks before 2s timeout
starvation_reference.finding: CONFIRMED: MMC >= 100 collapses throughput to ~34 TPS regardless of setting

mmc_tuning_effect.conclusion: MMC tuning shows a small effect (~5%), marginal at n=3. The ranges do not overlap (MMC=10 tops at 125.02, MMC=50 bottoms at 128.00), suggesting a real but modest improvement. The practical conclusion is unchanged: MaxMessageCount tuning buys roughly 5%, not an order of magnitude, and the single-orderer configuration is the binding constraint.

starvation_finding.statement: At MMC >= 100, throughput collapses to ~34 TPS due to batch starvation (blocks cut by timeout, not message count)

single_orderer_constraint.statement: The single-orderer configuration is the likely constraint. Raft requires minimum 3 orderers for fault-tolerant deployment; this test uses 1.
single_orderer_constraint.implication: Production deployments should expect different scaling characteristics

corrected_conclusion.t56_correction: T56 claimed MMC=50 was optimal (131 TPS vs 120 TPS). With 3 runs per config, MMC=50 shows a small (~5%) improvement over MMC=10, marginal at n=3 (p~0.06). The practical conclusion: throughput ceiling is ~119-133 TPS; MMC tuning provides modest gains but the single-orderer configuration is the binding constraint.
